Settings

Display
Silkscreen OFL · titles, scores and labels; snap to multiples of 8 px
Text
Rubik OFL
Mono
Pixelify Sans OFL · mid-size headings where Silkscreen is too blocky
Moves
bitmap display, tight setting
Mood
nostalgic, playful, crisp, competitive
Case
Pixel titles in capitals at 8 px multiples (16, 32, 48, 96); headings in sentence case in the softer pixel face; body in Rubik.
Numerals and features
font-smooth: never; -webkit-font-smoothing: none; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums

P1 001200 · P2 000800P1 001200 · P2 000800

Pixel faces only look crisp at whole multiples of their grid; set sizes on 8 px steps and turn smoothing off.
Signature
A pixel title that steps in once like a cartridge boot (a hard 4-frame reveal, no easing), then holds; everything readable stays in Rubik.
Use when
Games, game tools, indie software, music and club nights, nostalgia campaigns.
Turns into slop when
When body copy is set in pixels, when the pixel face is scaled to odd sizes and blurs, or when a CRT glow and scanlines are added by reflex.
Offline
Without network the page falls back to the system stacks in --f-display and --f-text; no font files ship with this specimen.
Specimen copy is placeholder text written for this library; it describes no real product or result.
